method: Match specific live claims to original source passages. Primary texts/abstracts consulted at specified locators; PDFs with page images unavailable are explicitly limited. Findings cover listed claims only, not all references, all debate stages or published theological certification.

cases.en: VS §53 distinguishes enduring universal norms from new formulations adapted to circumstances; §§78–82 reject judging an intrinsically wrong chosen object good because of intentions or outcomes.
cases.fr: VS §53 distingue la norme universelle permanente des formulations adaptées aux circonstances ; les §§78–82 refusent qu'une intention ou des conséquences transforment un objet intrinsèquement mauvais en acte bon.
cases.limit: Does not certify an unnamed teaching as definitively proposed by the Church, nor does it establish the correctness of every future application to emerging technologies or particular sexual practices.

cases.risk: traditional marriage hierarchy versus later reciprocal submission
cases.en: Casti Connubii §26 explicitly asserts husbandly primacy and wife's willing obedience, §27 protects her freedom and rejects unreasonable demands; Mulieris Dignitatem §24 explicitly says spousal subjection is mutual and regards gospel reciprocity as an innovation.
cases.fr: Casti Connubii (§26) affirme expressément la primauté du mari et la soumission volontaire de l'épouse, tandis que le §27 protège sa liberté ; Mulieris Dignitatem (§24) affirme explicitement la soumission mutuelle comme nouveauté évangélique.
cases.limit: Neither document explicitly supplies a universal procedural casting vote for all family decisions; no full theological reconciliation of the two magisterial formulations certified.

cases.en: Humanae Vitae §13 expressly rejects intercourse imposed disregarding a spouse's condition and reasonable wishes; Aquinas q.64 a.1 treats the mutual duty as real but calls a demand that endangers the other's bodily welfare unjust.
cases.fr: Humanae Vitae (§13) rejette expressément l'union imposée sans égard à l'état et aux désirs légitimes du conjoint ; saint Thomas limite le devoir réciproque lorsqu'une demande compromet le bien corporel de l'autre.
cases.limit: Neither a reciprocal moral debt nor traditional headship constitutes permission for sexual force; treatment of specific clinical/trauma circumstances remains case-dependent.

cases.en: McHugh–Callan §1624(a) distinguishes non-consummated marital affection fostering conjugal love from deliberate non-conjugal sexual completion and chosen proximate occasions of that completion.
cases.fr: McHugh–Callan (§1624 a) distingue les gestes conjugaux non consommés qui entretiennent l'amour des époux de l'achèvement sexuel délibéré hors de l'acte conjugal.
cases.limit: The manual gives no direct ruling on every modern device; retrieved original extracted PDF text, but page-image screenshot attempt failed. Archived case, not publication-ready or fully verified.

cases.risk: specific anal sexual acts / archived question
cases.en: Classical moral theology distinguishes acts consummated outside the conjugal act from preparatory acts, but the precise permission claim about particular anal acts is not established merely by a general treatment of incomplete acts.
cases.fr: La théologie morale classique distingue l'achèvement sexuel hors de l'acte conjugal et certains gestes préparatoires ; une permission précise de pratiques anales ne découle pas de cette règle générale.
cases.limit: Specific act-by-act magisterial adjudication and original contextual proof remain outstanding. Never promote this archived question as a certified general permission.

cases.risk: frozen embryo disposition and prenatal adoption
cases.en: Dignitas Personae §19 condemns destruction for research and embryo transfer as an infertility treatment; it treats prenatal adoption as praiseworthy in intent but morally problematic rather than explicitly declaring every conceivable rescue scenario categorically condemned.
cases.fr: Dignitas Personae (§19) rejette la destruction pour la recherche et le transfert comme traitement de la stérilité ; l'adoption prénatale est louable dans son intention, mais soulève des difficultés morales sérieuses.
cases.limit: The instruction does not prescribe a universally licit intervention for already frozen embryos; do not classify a disputed rescue practice as officially approved or uniformly condemned.

cases.en: Aquinas differentiates exteriorly compelled bodily movements from interior willing; the 2024 scoping review found physiological genital response can occur in non-consensual activity among 136 male and 250 female survivors in its included sources.
cases.fr: Saint Thomas distingue l'acte corporel subi par contrainte du consentement intérieur ; la revue exploratoire de 2024 confirme la possibilité de réponses génitales sans consentement dans les données recensées.
cases.limit: The review could not estimate prevalence or circumstances and does not decide individual guilt, a legal consent threshold or all trauma physiology.

cases.en: Aquinas q.151 a.1 reply 2 directly cites Augustine that another's sexual violence cannot remove chastity where the victim's will does not consent; q.6 treats violence as causing involuntariness in exterior acts.
cases.fr: Saint Thomas (II–II, q.151, a.1, ad 2) reprend saint Augustin : la violence sexuelle subie sans consentement de la volonté ne détruit pas la chasteté de la victime.
cases.limit: Physical sensation is neither proof of consent nor personal guilt. An internal voluntary act, if any, is not inferred from involuntary arousal.

cases.en: Aquinas says violence directly opposes the voluntary and that actions under fear can be mixed, partly voluntary and involuntary; fear does not automatically remove all voluntariness.
cases.fr: Saint Thomas enseigne que la violence s'oppose directement au volontaire et que les actes commis sous la peur peuvent mêler volontaire et involontaire ; la peur ne supprime donc pas automatiquement toute imputabilité.
cases.limit: Do not claim any level of fear uniformly cancels culpability or that compliance under threat necessarily constitutes freely given sexual consent.

cases.en: Canon 988 concerns an individual's own grave sins; it does not make a person responsible for violence committed against them. Aquinas explicitly preserves chastity under violence where the will refuses consent.
cases.fr: Le canon 988 oblige à confesser ses propres péchés graves, et non les violences subies ; saint Thomas maintient la chasteté de la personne dont la volonté n'a pas consenti à l'agression.
cases.limit: Neither canon law nor moral theology warrants presuming sin from a survivor's freezing, involuntary bodily response or failure to resist.

cases.en: The 1974 CDF declaration §§12–14 protects life from fertilization and states the moral norm does not depend on resolving philosophical ensoulment debates; it explicitly declines to make biological science settle personhood.
cases.fr: La déclaration de la CDF de 1974 (§§12–14) protège la vie dès le commencement et distingue l'interdiction de l'avortement d'une certitude philosophique sur l'instant exact de l'animation.
cases.limit: Does not establish that developmental stages have identical functioning or that genetics alone resolves the philosophical question of personhood.

cases.en: The 1974 declaration recognizes grave hardship but rejects the direct taking of innocent life; the 2009 CDF text explicitly repeats the absolute norm for direct abortion amid difficult and tragic circumstances.
cases.fr: La déclaration de 1974 reconnaît les difficultés graves, sans admettre la suppression directe d'une vie innocente ; la CDF réaffirme en 2009 cette norme même dans les circonstances tragiques.
cases.limit: This is a moral prohibition of direct abortion, not a denial of rape trauma, physical danger or the duties of society towards the victim.

primary: 2013 National Catholic Bioethics Center original PDF pp. 1–2; three distinct ectopic methods and explicit absence of procedure-specific magisterial ruling
cases.en: The 2009 CDF text explicitly distinguishes directly causing fetal death from maternal treatment that has unintended collateral fetal death, citing Pius XII's 1951 conditions; the National Catholic Bioethics Center distinguishes debate over particular ectopic procedures.
cases.fr: La CDF distingue en 2009 la mort directement voulue de l'enfant et un soin maternel dont elle serait l'effet secondaire non voulu, selon les conditions précisées par Pie XII en 1951.
cases.limit: Neither the CDF statement nor the non-magisterial NCBC FAQ provides a magisterial licence for salpingostomy or methotrexate. NCBC pp. 1–2 inspected in original document and page 2 visually cross-checked; urgent medical assessment must not be delayed.

cases.en: Veritatis Splendor §§78–82 distinguishes the object of the deliberately chosen act from further intentions and consequences; §81 denies that a good motive makes an intrinsically evil object good.
cases.fr: Veritatis Splendor (§§78–82) distingue l'objet choisi des intentions et des conséquences, et exclut qu'un bon motif rende moralement bon un acte intrinsèquement mauvais.
cases.limit: Distinguish objective moral species from a person's subjective guilt and pastoral disposition; the encyclical does not assess a particular person's culpability.
